question: Separate sponsored-project grants from grants to a host's own programmes. For the 25 largest Fiscal Sponsor Directory hosts by top-50 Schedule I dollars (e.g. 50CAN $94.2m, Global Impact $51.5m, NEO Philanthropy $47.5m, King Baudouin Foundation US $46.5m), read each host's Form 990 (Part III programme descriptions; Schedule I/F outflows) and the sponsors' Schedule I purpose text, and estimate the share of DAF dollars that pass through to sponsored projects
conclusion_affected: Fiscal-sponsor component of the exception proxy (now 0.44% of lines, 1.94% of dollars); whether the 4.4x dollar-to-count ratio is a fiscal-sponsorship effect or a host-size effect
rationale: A host's EIN appearing on the directory does not mean every grant to it funds a sponsored project. Several directory hosts run large programmes of their own, so the EIN-keyed flag is an upper bound for the hosts added by the directory ($557m)

question: Key the 76 Fiscal Sponsor Directory hosts left unmatched (71) or ambiguous (5) to EINs: fetch each listing page on fiscalsponsordirectory.org (robots.txt allows all paths) for street address and ZIP, and match on BMF name + ZIP; report the change in the fiscal-sponsor share
conclusion_affected: Completeness of the EIN-keyed fiscal-sponsor list
rationale: 337 of 413 directory hosts were keyed from the alpha list's name, city and state, plus EINs that sponsors reported on Schedule I. Unmatched hosts include DBAs and renamed organisations, e.g. The Gotham Film & Media Institute and Maysles Documentary Center. Their Schedule I footprint is unknown

question: Derive de facto fiscal sponsors from the filings themselves: across all top-50 Schedule I lines, find recipient EINs that appear under 'X FBO Y', 'X c/o Y' or 'X on behalf of Y' names for at least three distinct projects, then compare that set with the directory and Q-B15 hosts
conclusion_affected: Fiscal-sponsor share; whether the directory misses large hosts that do not list themselves
rationale: The NNFS member directory is rendered by a third-party script (communitybox.co) and is not in the page HTML, so it could not be used. Sponsors' own Schedule I names already carry FBO/c/o project markers (e.g. 'TIDES CENTER FBO ...', 'SOCIAL GOOD FUND FBO ...'), which give a filing-based list

question: Classify the 3,047 'newly listed church' recent-ruling lines ($356.1m). Using BMF FOUNDATION code 10, Pub 78 and the e-file index, test whether these are churches that obtained a first determination letter voluntarily (no review need) or new congregations; decide whether they belong in the new-grantee cohort
conclusion_affected: Size of the true new-grantee cohort (19,231 lines / $4.38bn after the split)
rationale: Churches need no application, so a first BMF ruling month does not date the church. These lines are split out but not removed from the time-correct recent flag

question: Close the archive gap before 2023-06: for FY2023 grant years ending 2023-03 to 2023-05, find a dated BMF of 2023-01 to 2023-05 (NCCS raw/bmf returns 403 for those months; web.archive.org was unreachable from this session) and re-run the as-of classification for the 336 lines ($121.4m) that rest on a snapshot taken at least three months after the year end
conclusion_affected: Time-correct recent-ruling flag for FY2023 March to May year ends
rationale: The first usable monthly archive is 2023-06 (2023-08 is truncated and dropped). Rulings dated before the year end are unaffected; only resets posted in the lag window could be misread

question: Propagate the refined proxy into gap19-exception-load-proxy.md §0 and DAF-INDUSTRY-REPORT-2026-11.md §4. Core is 7.76% of lines and 11.61% of dollars, or 6.80% / 11.00% counting only true new organisations; the fiscal-sponsor dollar-to-count ratio is 4.4x, not 10.7x; the time-correct recent ruling is 4.14% / 5.34%
conclusion_affected: 'About 7% of lines and 10-11% of dollars' (core proxy); the claim that fiscal-sponsor grants are the most dollar-heavy category
rationale: Both refinements move the headline only modestly, but they change the composition. Fiscal sponsors go from 0.12% to 0.44% of lines; 2,561 recent-ruling lines ($411.4m) were not recent at grant time; and 3,047 lines are newly listed churches rather than new organisations
